entries.title: Fibres and glasses are competing material states in protein condensation
entries.summary: Nature Physics, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03415-z Fibres are thought to emerge from a dense protein condensate ageing into a glassy state. It is now shown that protein fibres and glassy condensates may result from two competing ageing pathways.

entries.title: A liquid-crystal analogue of the skyrmion Hall effect
entries.summary: Nature Physics, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03379-0 Magnetic skyrmions are known to exhibit a Hall effect in the presence of an electric current. Now it is shown that liquid-crystal solitons also exhibit a Hall-like drift under shear flow.

entries.title: Experiment shows when quantum 'cat' states stop bouncing back
entries.summary: Quantum systems can occupy superpositions, quantum states that combine different possibilities. For instance, a microwave field can be prepared in a superposition of an empty state and a state that contains microwave light.
